input.title: Hip fracture surgery bill for my grandmother Kamakshi Venugopal
input.story: My grandmother Kamakshi Venugopal, 78, slipped in the bathroom at our home in Thanjavur on 29 October 2026 and broke her left hip. She was admitted to Sri Raghavendra Ortho Care Hospital the same day and had a hip replacement (hemiarthroplasty) on 1 November 2026. She was discharged on 8 November 2026 and is recovering with physiotherapy at home. We paid ₹40,000 as an advance from our savings. The remaining bill of ₹1,84,600 has to be settled within 30 days under the undertaking I signed at discharge. I am Arun Venugopal, her grandson. The money will be paid directly to the hospital.

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.content:
Sri Raghavendra Ortho Care Hospital, Thanjavur
Discharge Summary - Date: 08/11/2026
Patient: Kamakshi Venugopal, 78 F, IP No. SROC/IP/5521
Date of admission: 29/10/2026. Diagnosis: displaced fracture of the neck of the left femur. Procedure: left cemented bipolar hemiarthroplasty on 01/11/2026 under spinal anaesthesia. Post-operative course uneventful; mobilised with a walker. Discharged on 08/11/2026 in stable condition. Review in orthopaedic OPD after two weeks with a check X-ray.

documents.title: Final bill
documents.content:
Sri Raghavendra Ortho Care Hospital, Thanjavur
Final Bill No. SROC/FB/2093, Bill date: 08/11/2026
Patient: Kamakshi Venugopal, IP No. SROC/IP/5521
Room charges (10 days) ₹38,000; bipolar prosthesis (implant) ₹78,500; surgeon and anaesthesia fees ₹52,000; theatre and consumables ₹31,600; pharmacy and investigations ₹24,500. Gross total ₹2,24,600. Less advance received on 29/10/2026: ₹40,000. Balance payable: ₹1,84,600. The hospital has accepted a written undertaking from the patient's grandson, Arun Venugopal, to settle the balance within 30 days of discharge.

documents.title: X-ray report
documents.content:
Thanjavur Diagnostic Centre
Report date: 29/10/2026
Patient: Kamakshi Venugopal, 78 F. Referred by: casualty, Sri Raghavendra Ortho Care Hospital.
X-ray of the pelvis with both hips (AP view): displaced subcapital fracture of the left femoral neck. No other bony injury seen.

input.title: Second-year veterinary college fees for Harpreet Kaur Sandhu
input.story: I am Harpreet Kaur Sandhu, a second-year veterinary student at Satluj College of Veterinary Sciences, Ludhiana. My father is a small dairy farmer and lost most of his herd to lumpy skin disease this year. The college has asked for ₹1,47,000 for tuition, hostel, mess and examination fees for this year. I have attached the fee demand notice, my bonafide certificate and our family income certificate. The money will be paid to the college accounts office.

input.story: My younger brother Rohan Mehta, 24, was admitted to Narmada Lifeline Hospital in Vadodara with severe dengue on 2 November 2026 and spent five days in the ICU. He was discharged on 11 November 2026, but the hospital is holding his discharge papers until we pay the final bill of ₹2,36,800. We are a family of daily-wage workers and cannot pay this amount. input.title: Cleft palate repair for baby Mehrunissa Bhat
input.story: Our daughter Mehrunissa Bhat is 11 months old and was born with a cleft palate, which makes feeding very difficult. The paediatric plastic surgery team at Jhelum Children's Hospital in Srinagar has planned her palate repair for 5 December 2026. She has a pre-anaesthetic check on 28 November 2026 and will be admitted on 4 December 2026. The hospital estimate is ₹1,12,500. My husband Tariq Bhat rows a shikara and our income stops in winter. The funds will be paid directly to the hospital.

input.title: Animal ambulance van for Karuna Paws Rescue Trust, Nashik
input.story: Karuna Paws Rescue Trust runs a 60-animal shelter on Trimbak Road on the outskirts of Nashik and answers about 90 road-accident calls a month for stray dogs, cattle and birds. Today we carry injured animals in an autorickshaw. We are raising ₹6,40,000 for a small animal ambulance fitted with a stretcher, oxygen and a cage. Our trust registration, the board resolution and the body-builder's quotation are attached. Funds will be paid to the dealer against the invoice.

input.title: Braille textbooks and a slate for Class 9 student Lalrinpuii
input.story: Lalrinpuii is a 14-year-old Class 9 student at Government High School, Chaltlang, in Aizawl. She lost her sight to glaucoma two years ago and now studies in Braille, but the school only has Braille books up to Class 7. Her teacher estimates that the Class 9 science, mathematics and social science textbooks in Braille, a Braille slate and stylus, and a Taylor frame for mathematics will cost about ₹38,500. Her mother sells vegetables at Bara Bazar. We are still collecting the supplier's quotation.

This is to certify that Lalrinpuii, daughter of Lalthanzami, is a bonafide student of Class IX of this school for the current session. She is visually impaired and studies using Braille.

input.title: Urgent bypass surgery for my father Joseph Varghese
input.story: My father Joseph Varghese, 61, was found to have three blocked arteries after an angiogram at Meenachil Heart Institute in Kottayam. The cardiologist has told us he needs coronary bypass surgery urgently. The surgery and ICU stay will cost ₹5,60,000. We have attached his angiogram report and the hospital bill. Please donate to save his life.
